subject: psychology
title: Multi-Store Model: Capacity, Duration, Encoding
welcome_lead: How much, how long, in what code — STM and LTM compared.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology MSM capacity Miller 7±2 duration Peterson encoding Baddeley.
final_note: STM and LTM differ on three measurable axes.

concepts.def: Up to a lifetime (Bahrick 1975 yearbook study).

walkthroughs.body_html: Miller (1956) 'The Magical Number Seven': STM holds 7±2 chunks. Chunking groups items (CIA, FBI, IRS). Jacobs (1887): digit span averaged 9 for digits, 7 for letters. Cowan (2001) argues true capacity is closer to 4. LTM capacity is effectively unlimited.

Peterson & Peterson (1959): trigrams + counting backwards prevented rehearsal. After 3 sec ~80% recall; after 18 sec ~3% — STM duration ~18 seconds. Bahrick et al. (1975) tested 392 ex-students: 90% face recognition after 48 years — LTM lasts decades.

Baddeley (1966): STM struggled with acoustically similar words (cat-cap-can) — STM is acoustic. After 20 min, LTM struggled with semantically similar words (big-large-huge) — LTM is semantic. Different encoding supports separate stores.
